positive.reasoning: Criterion A1 (traumatic event): MET — patient confirmed experiencing a life-threatening situation a few months ago. Criterion B1 (intrusive thoughts): MET — patient reports frequent intrusive thoughts about the event. Criterion B2 (distressing dreams): MET — patient described having disturbing dreams related to the event. Criterion B3 (flashbacks): MET — patient experiences heightened alertness and discomfort when reminded of the event. Criterion C1 (avoidance of thoughts): MET — patient actively avoids thinking about the event. Criterion C2 (avoidance of reminders): MET — patient avoids places and conversations that remind them of the event. Criterion D1 (inability to recall details): MET — patient reports difficulty recalling important parts of the trauma. Criterion D2 (negative beliefs): MET — patient describes a more negative outlook on life since the event. Criterion D3 (blame): MET — patient often blames themselves for the trauma. Criterion D4 (negative emotions): MET — patient reports consistently negative feelings. Criterion D5 (diminished interest): MET — patient has lost interest in activities they once enjoyed. Criterion D6 (detachment): MET — patient feels detached from others. Criterion D7 (inability to experience positive emotions): MET — patient finds it hard to feel positive emotions. Criterion D8 (irritability): MET — patient reports increased irritability. Criterion D9 (recklessness): MET — patient describes engaging in risky behaviors. Criterion E1 (hypervigilance): MET — patient feels constantly on guard. Criterion E2 (startle response): MET — patient is more easily startled. Criterion E3 (concentration): MET — patient has difficulty concentrating. Criterion E4 (sleep disturbance): MET — patient experiences difficulty sleeping. Criterion F (duration): MET — symptoms began shortly after the event and have persisted for over a month. Criterion G (functional impairment): MET — symptoms cause significant distress and interfere with work and social interactions. Exclusion criteria: NOT MET — patient denies substance use or medical conditions affecting symptoms. Total: 20 of 20 criteria met (threshold ≥1). Diagnosis: TRUE — full criteria for PTSD are met with significant functional impairment confirmed.
